problem: Classical reinforcement-learning VLN policies reward mainly the change in distance to the target viewpoint, so object information in the instruction and the observations plays little role in the reward signal.
motivation: Aligning objects seen by the agent with objects named in the instruction is critical for following instructions. A reward that also reflects instruction-following progress should guide the agent better than a distance-only reward and generalize better to unseen environments.
key_idea: Shape the RL reward with both distance-to-goal change and instruction-progress estimated by aligning visually observed objects with objects mentioned at specific positions in the instruction.
insight: The abstract suggests that object-level visual-instruction alignment can serve as a proxy for navigation progress, giving a denser and more semantic reward than distance alone. No ablations are available because only the abstract was provided.
method: Reward shaping: combines the change in the agent's distance to the target with a navigation-progress term.
Object alignment: matches visual object information observed by the agent to object information specified in the instruction.
Progress estimation: uses the position of the aligned object within the instruction to estimate approximate progress along the instruction.
